analysis:
The supplied units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change; the patch excerpt shows only prose edits (onboarding stop handling around line 453 and other doc ranges). No executable code, keys, wire formats, or configuration are changed by the supplied files, so no concrete regression against the threat model is identified.

Examined content: cluster/MiMo/Qwen/Gemma/GPT-OSS batch decode descriptions, TP lane parity, saved-width placement, and Qwen media transport. Security-relevant statements are consistent with existing controls: the docs say that logs are size-only and contain no tokens or prompt text, that media/encoded bytes stay only in the request owner and rank 0 (A-001), that load agreements bind arithmetic and wire versions so mismatched ranks refuse to load, and that prefix reuse is off for the page paths or scoped per request partition. Both T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT oracle, SEC-035) and the sealed-pair requirement (an unkeyed TP load is refused) are unchanged in kind. The docs describe the prefix cache as using tenant partitions, but that doc is outside the supplied units, so the prefix-cache scoping claims for the TP batch owner (memory/SSD tiers keyed by each request's partition) should be checked against code in a later pass; the docs state the claim but the code is not supplied.

The documentation claims that no public qualification grants, lane defaults, or serving grants change (for example MiMo batch, Nemotron batch, Bonsai). This cannot be verified from the docs alone and is an unverified contract, not a finding. The build-ahead protocol is stated to be not yet on in the product. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the remaining doc changes (stop-count mechanics in onboarding) were only partly visible; they describe a local/pair control-plane stop count and appear to add no new trust boundary beyond what is already described.

Remaining integration questions: whether code changes elsewhere in the PR match these doc claims (selection non-finite check in the sealed sum, the folded-control wire version, the stop-count status reply authenticated between Macs).
